case_title.quote: PARGAN SINGH V. STATE OF PUNJAB & ANR.

number_of_accused.quote: the two appellant challenge the veracity

accused_gender.quote: two sikh gentlemen with trimmed beard
accused_gender.reason: Accused described as gentlemen, i.e. male.

accused_religion.quote: two sikh gentlemen with trimmed beard
accused_religion.reason: The judgment describes the assailants, i.e. the accused, as Sikh, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the two perpetrators of the aforesaid crime were sikh gentlemen but unknown to the complainant or other persons
accused_victim_relationship.reason: They were unknown to the witnesses, so strangers.

offence_category.quote: convicted the appellants under Section 302, 397 as well as Section 307 IPC

statutory_provisions.quote: under Section 302, 397 as well as Section 307 IPC read with Section 34 IPC

weapon.quote: started firing with pistol on Varun Kumar

evidence_type.quote: conviction is primarily based on the depositions of PW-1 to PW-3
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, confession and medical evidence are all present.

confession.quote: extra-judicial confession by its very nature is rather a weak type of evidence

aggravating_circumstances.quote: they had fired at PW-2 as well. For PW-2, it was clearly a horror scene
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Circumstances are drawn from the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.quote: rigorous imprisonment of life and fine of Rs.50,000/- each

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court has dismissed their appeals
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeals on 13.12.2012.

final_outcome.quote: these appeals are bereft of any merit and are accordingly dismissed

offence_finally_established.quote: sufficient to uphold the conviction of the appellants
offence_finally_established.reason: Convictions under ss.302, 307 and 397 with s.34 were upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life term, so null is acceptable.

neutral_facts.correct_value: The complainant Naveen Sharma and Varun Kumar withdrew Rs.4 lakh; Varun carried the bag. Two men on a scooter fired at Varun; the pillion rider snatched the bag and later fired at Kamaljit Singh, who tried to stop them.
neutral_facts.quote: Naveen Sharma ... Varun Kumar alias Kaka was accompanying him ... Varun Kumar placed the bag containing money in front of scooter
neutral_facts.reason: Muddles who withdrew the money and who was the companion. It also says the pillion rider fired at the victim, which the judgment does not clearly state.

attempt_completion.quote: seriousness of the injury has resulted into conviction under Section 307 IPC

physical_harm.quote: cause of death ... severe haemorrhage and shock and injury to vital organs
physical_harm.reason: Consistent with the post-mortem and PW-2's injuries.

number_of_offences.quote: framed the charges ... Section 302, 307 and 397 IPC

financial_property_loss.quote: withdrew a sum of Rs.4 lakhs ... snatched the money bag ... also having one cheque book

motive.quote: snatched the money bag from Varun Kumar

key_evidence_accepted.quote: even if ... we discard the testimony of PW-1, the evidence of two eye-witnesses ... is sufficient

witness_credibility.quote: testimony of an injured witness requires a higher degree of credibility

post_offence_conduct.quote: the accused declined the same through separate statements

custody_duration.reason: Duration of custody is not stated.

legal_representation.quote: A. Tiwari, Eliza Bar, Shree Pal Singh, Shiv kumar Suri, Shikhil Suri, for the Appellant

investigation_status.quote: challan against the appellants was presented before the Court

appeal_history.quote: High Court has dismissed their appeals ... Sessions Judge, Kapurthala

prosecution_argument.quote: 90 seconds was more than sufficient time for these witnesses to observe the assailants

defence_argument.quote: faces were shown to him, there could not have any purpose of Test Identification Parade

legal_principle_applied.quote: Whether a particular event or the faces of a person could be remembered would depend upon the circumstances

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Balwinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (1995) Supp (4) SCC 259

sentencing_rationale.reason: The Court gave no sentencing reasoning.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: For PW-2, it was clearly a horror scene resulting into traumatic experience.
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: This was reasoning on memory and identification, not stated as a sentencing aggravating factor.

other_sentence_order.quote: All these sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
other_sentence_order.reason: No other orders beyond concurrent running.
